prospect.name: Brandon Shpirt
prospect.occupation: Property management and real estate development business owner — started as a realtor, began with six units, now manages a few hundred doors and runs development projects including apartment builds. Sits at a desk essentially all day; had got up twice by the time of the call.
prospect.family_status: Married; wife is 5'4" and about 120 lb. First child due within weeks. Financially supports his own household and his parents' household.
prospect.training_background: Athletic and played sports through his early twenties, sitting around 195-205 lb. Lifestyle change in his mid-twenties — 6am to 8 or 9pm workdays plus a long commute — took him to 280 lb in about two years. Completed 75 Hard, dropping from 284 to 223 lb on roughly 1,600 calories a day with two workouts daily, then rebounded to 260. Currently not training at all; previous attempts were sporadic, a few weeks at a time. Has trained one-to-one at a boutique functional training facility in South Florida at about $1,500 a month and rated it highly. Avoids barbell work entirely because of his shoulders; uses neutral-grip dumbbells only. Plans to train in his garage. Self-describes as all-or-nothing.
prospect.medical: Two bulging discs in the lumbar spine. Two stretched ligaments in the knees from sports injuries when younger. Bilateral shoulder impingement he describes as a pinching, aggravated by sleeping on his arm and by returning to the gym 'too much too fast'. Chronic inflammation and pain — 'Even at 220, getting out of bed was painful' — with shoulders and lumbar the main sites. Says any pushing movement, overhead or chest, is compromised, and barbell loading of his back caused repeated flare-ups that put him 'out of commission for a while'. Reports the 75 Hard period produced wild systemic inflammation. Currently 265 lb at 6'0".

Carries visible regret about the rebound: 'I look back and I kick myself because it's like, I just could have kept going. I'd be in a different position than I am right now'

objections.raw_quote: I used to train with a, uh, during that 75. I had time. I was investing quite a lot of money into training. I was spending like $1,500 a month on training, but I had one-on-one training with a functional training facility... My issue is I'm going to spend plus or minus that same amount of money, and I'm not, I don't know if I'm getting that same one-on-one training. Right now I'm talking about an online program... I just don't know how I can get the same, again, from a business standpoint, dollar to dollar that I would with someone that I can physically see three, four times a week.
objections.rep_response: Countered on three fronts without a script: expertise scarcity ('there are not a lot of people in this space who are actually experts on kettlebells, like real experts'), time efficiency, and equipment minimalism ('with kettlebells, you will only need one thing and one thing only, which is just the kettlebell'). He never did the arithmetic the prospect had handed him — $1,500 a month for six months is $9,000 against $6,000 — so the 'same money' premise went unchallenged.

objections.raw_quote: So let's do this. Give me until tomorrow and I'll give you a response if I want to move forward or not.
objections.rep_response: Asked one good scripted question — 'What's coming up that you don't want to go forward right now?' — which surfaced the real value objection, and later 'what's going to be the main factor that's going to pull the scale to one or to the other', which surfaced that he intends to re-approach his old trainers. Then accepted the deferral, let the prospect set the deadline himself and closed the call.

objections.raw_quote: in a lot of businesses, some people take full payments up front, and then the communication falls off. And I just want to make sure things like that don't happen... I'm in the construction world where I leave 10% hanging on every contract until I get completion at the very end... Why? Because if I pay them in full, it's going to take them three business days to respond to my phone call.
objections.rep_response: Immediately volunteered a 50/50 split with no interest — 'Look, Brandon, you're a business guy. I'm a business guy too. If you want to split it in half, that's fine with me. There's no interest on that.' Offered before the prospect asked for it and without any of the financial-picture questions.

offer.payment_plan_terms: A 50/50 split offered unprompted with interest explicitly waived: 'If you want to split it in half, that's fine with me. There's no interest on that.' No amounts, dates or mechanism were established because the prospect deferred.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: "there's also a guarantee from him that in those six months, you will add at least eight kilos, which is like 17 pounds, to your core kettlebell movements"

evidence: Explicit deferral with a self-set deadline: 'Give me about a day or two... no later than Friday, I'll let you know what's up for sure.'
Not a no — 'this may be that, that's why I'm not saying no' and 'It's not that I'm against spending the $6,000.'

Counter-evidence on likelihood: he named his alternative and his intention to pursue it first — 'I'm going to reach out to those same trainers... if I can set up something that's more favorable for me there, I would rather do that.'
No payment taken, no onboarding booked, no follow-up call scheduled. The only next step is a WhatsApp message from the rep and a promised answer by Friday.
outcome.next_step: Rep to message on WhatsApp; prospect to give a yes or no by Friday after re-approaching his former in-person functional training facility to see whether he can negotiate more favourable terms there.

notable.note: Two things stand out. First, the clinical picture — two bulging lumbar discs, bilateral shoulder impingement, stretched knee ligaments, 265 lb, and a stated history of a return to training causing injury — was fully disclosed and never routed to a clinician, while the rep presented a guarantee of adding 8kg to his core kettlebell movements. Second, this is the second interest-free instalment offer from this rep in two days, made the day after his manager told him in a 1-1 that payment plans are supposed to carry interest. The value objection was also winnable on the prospect's own numbers and was not: he compared $6,000 against a trainer he paid $1,500 a month, which is $9,000 over the same six months, and the rep never said so.
